lines.prompt: Report the D input logic of the flip-flops to report any existing enable or hold structures implemented through multiplexers or AND gates.

golden.reference: Report of enable/hold structures in DFF D-input logic. Official count UNKNOWN, but reliable-team score arithmetic RULES OUT 1796 (Team3), 1474 (Team4) and 1817 (Team7); remaining candidates are 721 (non-authoritative Team2 run) or an unobserved value (netlist self-loop count is 2213). Line 8 must be self-consistent with the team's own line 7.
golden.notes: Observed values: Team2-exchange-log=721, Team4=1474, Team3=1796, Team7=1817. Team2 caveat: the exchanged Team2 log is a DIFFERENT RUN than the graded one, so score-based reasoning about 721 is INVALID; 721 is only evidence of a plausible answer. Score arithmetic on reliable teams (Team3/Team4/Team7 all 9/11, each losing exactly 2 points): their answers are equivalent on every other line except the line-10 cone size (29 vs 22, which cannot be the differentiator since Team3 and Team4/Team7 scored identically), so the only consistent assignment is that all three lost lines 7 AND 8 — hence 1796, 1474 and 1817 are all NOT the official count. CORRECTED netlist facts (verified by independent traversal of test91.v): 2213 of the 2585 DFFs DO have their own Q in their combinational D-input cone (self-loop hold structures) — the earlier claim of zero was wrong. Team7's 1817 = DFFs whose D is driven by a NAND ((EN&DATA)|(!EN&Q) NAND-mux pattern), and 1817 + Team7's 396 exclusions = 2213 exactly. D-driver histogram: NAND 1817, NOR 279, OR 275, NOT 106, direct DFF-Q 106, PI/const 2. Official pattern definition and count remain unknown; grade via llm_judge for a reasonable enable/hold report, treating 721 and 2213 as the only unrefuted numeric candidates.
